tagline.text: A west-facing sunset beach just south of El Nido Town

location.label: Location
location.text: Corong-Corong, El Nido, Palawan (Bacuit Bay shore south of El Nido Town)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (per person, including transport, food and drinks)

children.text: Corong-Corong Beach is a long, curving west-facing beach on Bacuit Bay, just south of El Nido Town. Rather than dazzling white sand, its appeal is the sunset, the beachfront restaurants and a convenient location, which make it a good base for an El Nido trip.

Corong-Corong is a barangay (a village-level administrative district) right next to El Nido Town, and the long, curving beach along its waterfront is Corong-Corong Beach. El Nido Town sits under limestone cliffs, so the sun disappears behind them early, but Corong-Corong opens to the west and gives you a clear view of the sun setting over the sea. That is why travelers in El Nido gather here around dusk.

To be honest, this is not the most beautiful beach in El Nido. Beach guides say it is not as pristine and quiet as Nacpan or Duli, and many reviews complain that the water is shallow and full of boats, which makes it a letdown for swimming. In return, guesthouses, resorts, seafood grills, sunset bars, ATMs and convenience stores line the shore, so it is a comfortable place to stay and enjoy the evening. Travelers who know the area sometimes call it El Nido Town's everyday local beach.

Corong-Corong also serves as a departure point for island hopping tours. Boats for Tours A to D sometimes leave from this shore, and El Nido's long-distance bus and van terminal is in this barangay too. Keep in mind that if you arrive by van from Puerto Princesa, Corong-Corong is where you first get off.

This guide covers the atmosphere of the beach, the best sunset spots, what to know about swimming, how to get to and from town, tips for lodging and meals, the weather by season, and nearby sights that pair well with it. Prices differ between sources, so please confirm them again on site.

The biggest draw of Corong-Corong Beach is the sunset. As the sun sinks into the sea to the west, the silhouettes of the islands offshore and of the boats are tinted along with the sky, which makes for great photos. Sunset times change with the season, so check the time that day and head out about 30 minutes early.

blocks.title: Choosing your spot, from the middle to the far left

children.text: One sunset guide recommends the middle of the beach or the far left end as you face the sea, while another says the view from the southern end is better. Sit in the middle if you want to be on the sand, or walk toward either end if you prefer somewhere quieter. Helicopter Island offshore anchors the scenery.

blocks.title: Restaurants and sunset bars along the beach

children.text: Along the beach you will find open-air restaurants serving grilled seafood, places serving Filipino dishes and Italian and Mediterranean food, cafés with vegetarian options, and sunset bars. Tables fill up fast at sunset, so it is safer to reserve ahead in peak season.

blocks.title: Walking the sand flats at low tide

children.text: At low tide, wide stretches of sand and mudflat appear offshore and you can walk on them. According to reviews, at low tide you can even walk along the coast south to Marimegmeg (Las Cabañas) Beach. The bottom can be rough with stones and glass fragments, though, so wear sandals or water shoes.

blocks.title: Island hopping departures and boats to Seven Commandos

children.text: Island hopping tour boats leave from the Corong-Corong shore, and one guide says a round-trip boat from here to Seven Commandos Beach costs about ₱700–800, and another lists about ₱800 per person. Kayaks reportedly rent from about ₱400 per day, but it is dangerous to be paddling back after dark, so check sea conditions and return early.

blocks.title: A stay area close to El Nido Town

children.text: Lodging ranges from beachfront resorts to hillside villas and hostels. You can stay somewhere quieter than the town and still head in by tricycle when needed, which suits travelers who find the bustle of the town tiring.

blocks.title: Easy access to the bus and van terminal

children.text: El Nido's bus and van terminal is in Corong-Corong, so it is close and convenient on the day you leave for or arrive from Puerto Princesa. If you are carrying a lot of luggage, choosing a place to stay nearby makes getting around much easier.

items.title: Half day centered on sunset
items.subtitle: From an afternoon stroll to dusk

children.text: Reach Corong-Corong from El Nido Town by tricycle or on foot. The walk takes about 15–20 minutes. Stroll along the beach and scout out restaurants and spots you like.
Rest at a café or beachfront restaurant with a drink and a light snack. Seats fill up quickly around sunset, so grab a window or sand-side spot early.
Time your move to the sunset: head to the middle of the beach or a sandy spot at one end and watch the setting sun and the silhouettes of the islands offshore.
After the sun goes down, have dinner of grilled seafood or Filipino dishes, then return to town or your lodging by tricycle.
Sunset times vary by season, so check that day's time first.

items.title: Full day
items.subtitle: Combining island hopping with a sunset dinner

children.text: Board a hopping boat at the tour desk and set off on one of Tours A to D. Follow the instructions of the operator you booked for the route and departure point.
After the tour, return to the Corong-Corong area, shower at your lodging and rest.
Come out to the beach to watch the sunset and enjoy a drink at a sunset bar.
Have dinner at a beachfront restaurant or one in town. There are more restaurants in town, so you can go back and forth by tricycle.
Tour times and prices vary by operator and weather, so check before booking.

El Nido has its best weather and sea conditions in the dry season, from November to May. In this period the western sky is often clear, so you are more likely to see a sunset, and the water off Corong-Corong is relatively calm.

In the rainy season, from June to October, rain and wind increase, and island hopping tours may be cancelled or boats may be unable to go out. If you want to watch the sunset from the beach, check the weather forecast and keep your schedule flexible.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: A great time for both sunsets and island hopping; it is peak season, so book lodging and restaurants ahead.
The sea is calm and sunsets are often vivid, but midday is very hot.
Hopping may be cancelled and many days have no sunset view. Lodging rates are lower.

Corong-Corong offers beachfront resorts, hillside villas, hostels and guesthouses. If you want to watch the sunset from your room right on the water, choose a beachside place; if you want a quiet view, pick one on the hill. In peak season it is safest to book early, and since noise levels and beach conditions vary by review, check recent comments.

For meals you can choose grilled seafood and Filipino dishes, Italian and Mediterranean food, and vegetarian menus at beachfront restaurants, and sunset bars are good for a drink as the sun goes down. Most amenities are concentrated in El Nido Town, though, so go into town if you want shopping or more variety in restaurants. There are ATMs and convenience stores on the beach side, but bring cash in advance.
Secure your spot 30 minutes before sunset. Popular restaurants need reservations in peak season.
If you want to swim, the time when the tide is in is better. At low tide the bottom is shallow and rough, making swimming difficult.
If you plan to walk the flats at low tide or walk to Marimegmeg, wear sandals or water shoes.
If you want to swim in clean water, an island hopping tour or another beach such as Nacpan is a better choice.
If your lodging is not on the beach, it is safer to travel by tricycle at night. Arrange your ride back in advance.
Bring cash and insect repellent; insects can increase on the beach around sunset.
If you are taking a van to Puerto Princesa, check the schedule a day ahead and allow plenty of time to get to the terminal.
At low tide the bottom is shallow, may have stones and glass fragments, and has many boats, so it is not suitable for swimming.
When walking the beach at low tide, protect your feet and watch for sharp objects.
Some reviews say the area near the small river at the north end of the beach is not clean, so check conditions before heading there.
When kayaking, return before sunset and wear a life vest.
Fares differ between sources, so agree on the price before you ride.
In the rainy season, waves and wind can suspend boat service, so check the latest announcements.
